html:
A Persian lyric poet who lived almost all his life in Shiraz in southern Iran, in the 1300s. His collected poems, the Divan, are among the most loved books in the Persian language.

Hafez wrote mostly ghazals, short poems of love and wine. They can be read as earthly, as mystical in the manner of Sufism, or as both at once, and they mock hypocrite preachers. He served as a court poet under the shifting rulers of Shiraz, who rose and fell during his life. A famous story has him meeting Timur, who took Shiraz in 1387, but it is probably a legend.

His Divan sits in many Iranian homes beside the Quran. People open it at random for guidance, a custom called fal-e Hafez, and quote his lines as proverbs. His tomb in Shiraz is a place of visits.

In Europe he inspired Goethe, whose West-Eastern Divan answers him, and he joined Rumi and Ferdowsi as the Persian poets the world knows best.
